# Target release

**Target**: CASE/UCO 1.5.0

# Background

Structured operating system logging frameworks — Apple Unified Logging (OSLog), Windows ETW / Windows Event Log, and Linux systemd-journald — attach a common set of structured routing and correlation fields to every record: an emitting subsystem (Apple subsystem / ETW provider / journald `SYSLOG_IDENTIFIER` or `_SYSTEMD_UNIT`), a category or channel within that subsystem, a log level (Default/Info/Debug/Error/Fault; ETW levels; syslog priorities), an activity or correlation identifier for tracing related records across processes, and the sending image (library/binary) that emitted the record. `uco-observable:EventRecordFacet` models a generic log row (`eventRecordText`, `eventRecordServiceName`, `eventID`, times) but has no typed properties for these fields, so today they can only be captured as free-text or ad-hoc DictionaryEntry keys — unqueryable across tools and not comparable across cases. A dedicated `OperatingSystemLogRecordFacet`, composable alongside `EventRecordFacet` on the same `EventRecord` observable, gives forensic tools a shared, typed vocabulary for the highest-value OS log fields.

Field semantics are grounded in Apple's os_log documentation (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/os/logging), Microsoft's ETW documentation (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/etw/about-event-tracing), and the systemd journal-fields specification (https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd.journal-fields.html).

# Requirements

## Requirement 1

Define a new `OperatingSystemLogRecordFacet` Facet as a subclass of `uco-core:Facet`.

Properties:

- `logSubsystem` (xsd:string): The subsystem, provider, or unit that emitted the record (e.g., Apple OSLog subsystem 'com.apple.wifi', Windows ETW provider name, journald `_SYSTEMD_UNIT`).
- `logCategory` (xsd:string): The category or channel within the emitting subsystem (e.g., Apple OSLog category, Windows Event Log channel).
- `logLevel` (xsd:string): The severity or type of the record as reported by the logging framework (e.g., Default, Info, Debug, Error, Fault; ETW level; syslog priority).
- `activityIdentifier` (xsd:string): The activity, correlation, or tracing identifier grouping related records across processes (e.g., Apple OSLog activity ID, ETW ActivityId GUID).
- `senderImageName` (xsd:string): The name or path of the binary image (library or executable) that emitted the record (e.g., '/usr/libexec/wifid').

# Risk / Benefit analysis

## Benefits

- Gives Apple Unified Logging, Windows ETW/Event Log, and journald parsers one typed vocabulary for the routing/correlation fields every structured OS log carries, replacing ad-hoc DictionaryEntry keys.
- The same SPARQL query shape answers subsystem/level questions across platforms and across parsing tools.
- Composable with the existing `EventRecordFacet` on the same `EventRecord` — no changes to existing classes; fully backward-compatible.

## Risks

- Partial overlap with `EventRecordFacet.eventRecordServiceName` (which some tools use for the emitting process). Guidance text should distinguish the emitting process/service (`eventRecordServiceName`) from the logging framework's subsystem routing label (`logSubsystem`).
- `logLevel` values differ per framework; a free string is proposed rather than a controlled vocabulary to avoid privileging one platform's level names. A future vocabulary could tighten this.

# Competencies demonstrated

## Competency 1

An examiner parses `system_logs.logarchive` from an iOS 17.3 sysdiagnose with Mandiant `unifiedlog_iterator` and Lionel Notari's Unified Logs v2 SQLite tooling. Each row carries subsystem (`com.apple.wifi`), category (`dynamic`), log_type (`Default`), activity_id, and the sending library (`/usr/libexec/wifid`). The examiner wants one graph where a SPARQL query returns every Default-level record emitted by subsystem `com.apple.wifi` during the collection window, regardless of which parser produced the row — and wants the same query shape to work for a Windows ETW provider/channel or a journald unit in other cases.

### Competency Question 1.1

Which Default-level records were emitted by Apple OSLog subsystem `com.apple.wifi`, regardless of which parser produced the row?

#### Result 1.1

The wifid association record, with its message text and sending image, selected purely on typed facet properties.

### Competency Question 1.2

How many records did each subsystem/provider emit (the same query shape covering OSLog subsystems and ETW providers)?

#### Result 1.2

Per-subsystem record counts spanning `com.apple.wifi`, `com.apple.locationd.Core`, and `Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon` in one result set.

### Draft SPARQL

```sparql
PREFIX uco-observable: <https://ontology.unifiedcyberontology.org/uco/observable/>
PREFIX uco-core: <https://ontology.unifiedcyberontology.org/uco/core/>
PREFIX proposed: <http://example.org/ontology/proposed/>

SELECT ?record ?text ?sender
WHERE {
    ?record a uco-observable:EventRecord ;
            uco-core:hasFacet ?core , ?oslog .
    ?core a uco-observable:EventRecordFacet ;
          uco-observable:eventRecordText ?text .
    ?oslog a proposed:OperatingSystemLogRecordFacet ;
           proposed:logSubsystem "com.apple.wifi" ;
           proposed:logLevel "Default" ;
           proposed:senderImageName ?sender .
}
```

(The aggregate query for CQ 1.2 is in `change_proposals/operating-system-log-record-facet.sparql`.)

# Solution suggestion

* Define new class `OperatingSystemLogRecordFacet` as a subclass of `uco-core:Facet`
* Define property `logSubsystem` with range `xsd:string`
* Define property `logCategory` with range `xsd:string`
* Define property `logLevel` with range `xsd:string`
* Define property `activityIdentifier` with range `xsd:string`
* Define property `senderImageName` with range `xsd:string`
* Add SHACL shape for `OperatingSystemLogRecordFacet` with property constraints
* Add unit test(s) demonstrating valid and invalid usage

A prototype extension ontology used for pre-submission validation is at `change_proposals/operating-system-log-record-facet.ttl`.
